# How Should the Floating Base Velocity and Integration Be Verified When the LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED Frame Jacobian and Position Numerical Differentiation Are Inconsistent?

> **Current answer:** The original author confirmed that the floating base velocity, quaternion propagation, and integrator were processed in global coordinates, which is incompatible with the free-flyer local velocity required by the Pinocchio Jacobian. Alignment of local expressions yielded the expected result. The finite difference application q_plus = pin.integrate(model, q, v * eps) was performed on the configuration manifold, and the frame world position difference was used for comparison; the C++ output Jacobian should verify J is zeroed in advance.

## Key terms

- Floating base (free flyer) (浮动基)
- Local coordinates (局部坐标)
- Local coordinates world-aligned (LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED) (局部坐标世界轴对齐)
- Configuration manifold (配置流形)
- Finite difference (有限差分)

## Problem and symptoms

- Why is the Cartesian velocity from the LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED frame Jacobian not consistent with the numerical differentiation of the frame position?
- The blue solid line and purple dashed line in the first graph of the original post are clearly separated in multiple intervals.
- In the second graph, the real and dashed lines for most qdot are nearly coincident, indicating that not all numerical differentiation failed.

## Environment

- Pinocchio C++ getFrameJacobian and floating base system; the original post does not specify Pinocchio version, robot model, or operating system.

## Priority diagnostics

- Constructed the local configuration on the manifold using q_plus = pin.integrate(model, q, v * eps), and compared with the frame world position difference.
- Verify that the free-flyer base twist is provided in the local coordinate system as per Pinocchio, and do not directly pass global coordinate velocities.
- Ensure that J is zeroed in advance when using the output parameter in the C++ getFrameJacobian function.

## Possible causes

- The original author confirmed that their floating base velocity, quaternion propagation, and integrator were processed in global coordinates, which is incompatible with the free-flyer local velocity provided by Pinocchio.

## Attempts

- The project contributor provided a minimal Python code for the finite difference of pin.integrate and the frame velocity, Jv.
- There was an error in the explanation of getFrameVelocity during discussion, which was later corrected by the original reply; this card does not use the previously corrected old explanation.

## Effective fixes

- Align the floating base velocity, quaternion propagation, and integrator with the free-flyer local velocity required by Pinocchio; use pin.integrate instead of direct per-element differentiation for finite difference validation.

## Result

- The original author replied that the issue was resolved, and the alignment of coordinates yielded the expected result; the project contributor then closed the issue after the problem was resolved.
